missing_complete_lines.text: 6. Review the Text Artifact against everything loaded in step 5. Read each passage of reported speech as a review unit against the resolved language and genre guidance, preserving its meaning and distinctive voice; then cover the surrounding prose and the relations between passages. Record findings with the passage, requirement and what the reader loses. A finding against a headline, a standfirst or a subheading names that part and the defect in it — a claim the text does not carry, a heading from which a reader who sees only it cannot tell what the text is about, a subject named with nothing said about it, the opening it repeats — as a finding against any other passage names its defect, since that defect is what the delivery reports a repaired part by. For `article`, `casestudy`, `column` and `opinion`, the anatomy's counted limits are measured rather than read: run `uv run --no-cache --no-project "$LIBRARY/scripts/article_anatomy.py" -` with the complete Text Artifact on stdin, and take every count a finding reports from that output rather than from your own reading of the text. Exit 0 settles the counted requirements only: it says none of them is a finding, and nothing about the anatomy requirements the script does not count — whether the last section is an ending, whether the standfirst stands on its own, whether a subheading describes its section — which this review examines by reading the text, and step 11 reports the text as conforming to the anatomy only where every one of them was examined; exit 1 makes each requirement it names a finding; exit 2 says the script could not measure the text, so count the limits by hand and say in step 11's delivery that they were not machine-measured. A norm it reports is a finding only where `article-anatomy.review.md` says a departure from a *should* is one, and the `typical` figures it reports feed the whole-text reading that file describes, no single paragraph or section failing one of them. Read every `heading_pairs` entry against the full text and the loaded headline contract, including pairs with no `shared_words`: judge whether the two parts add different information in different wording. Necessary repeated names or topic words alone create no finding; a paraphrased repeat can be a finding with little or no overlap. Verify absent or ambiguous sentence estimates against the text, and inspect the pairs by hand on exit 2. Record a semantic echo with its pair, the headline requirement and what the reader loses, independently of structural conformance and exit status. For `pressrelease`, the two counted limits the genre states are measured the same way, with `--genre=pressrelease` before the `-`, and every count a finding reports comes from that output: exit 0 says neither limit is a finding and settles nothing else of the release, exit 1 makes each limit it names a finding, and exit 2 says the script found no level-1 heading or could not read the text, so count by hand and say in step 11's delivery that the limits were not machine-measured. That output carries no norms, `typical` figures or `heading_pairs`; read the headline and the summary against each other as the genre's review half says. A code sample — a fenced block, an indented block, or an inline code span — is quoted material rather than the text's own prose: its contents are read past rather than read against the rules, so nothing inside one is a finding and nothing inside one is changed, the docstrings, comments, and string literals among them. Prose about code is ordinary prose and is read like every other sentence. Judge only what is in front of you. What the artifact turns out to be is a finding and never a ground for declining to review it: a text that reads as a brief, an outline, or notes rather than a finished piece is reviewed against the resolved genre like any other, and that mismatch is a finding — ordinarily the first one — instead of a reason to stop, to hand the invocation back, or to propose another Skill in its place. Reaching that judgement reads no other Skill's instructions, neither a `SKILL.md` of theirs nor a `help.md`; the mechanical pass in step 9 is the one Skill this run ever follows. Without a selected brief, this Skill never compares the Text Artifact with source material, never asks for material it was not given, and never remarks that source verification was unavailable — Source Fidelity is the contract of the Skill that wrote the text, and a caveat about material nobody supplied is noise in every run that was not one. A contradiction, an unsupported claim, or an editorial defect visible inside the artifact itself is an ordinary finding. With a selected brief, also perform the question-by-question assessment in `brief-review.md` and merge its shortfalls and map conflicts into these findings. Done when the applicable reviews are complete.
